content: Moles are growths that appear on the skin. They form when melanocytes, which are pigment-producing cells in the skin, grow together in a cluster rather than being evenly distributed throughout the surrounding tissue. Moles are extremely common, and most individuals have between 10 and 40 moles on their body. It is not unusual for new moles to develop over time, particularly up until the age of 40. Moles typically appear in shades of pink, tan, or brown. They can either be flat or raised and are generally round or oval in shape. Most moles are no larger than the size of a pencil eraser. However, approximately one in ten people has at least one atypical mole, which is medically referred to as a dysplastic nevus. These atypical moles differ in appearance from ordinary moles and may have irregular features. Dysplastic nevi are of particular concern because they have a higher likelihood of developing into melanoma, a serious and potentially life-threatening form of skin cancer. For this reason, it is important to have any unusual moles evaluated by a healthcare professional. You should seek medical attention if a mole appears unusual, increases in size, changes in color or shape, or exhibits any other concerning changes.
